36.8 — Altered States, Dreams & Non-Ordinary Consciousness
Consciousness States Spectrum
Waking Normal baseline Beta/Alpha EEG
Hypnagogia Sleep onset theta, hallucinations
NREM Sleep Slow wave delta, repair
REM/Dreaming Active visual cx near-wake EEG
Lucid Dream Prefrontal active aware in dream
Meditation Alpha/Gamma default mode ↓
Psychedelic DMN disrupted hyperconnectivity
Dream Theories Freudian (wish-fulfilment): Dreams = disguised unconscious wishes Latent vs manifest content Activation-synthesis (Hobson): Brainstem activates randomly during REM Cortex constructs narrative from noise Threat simulation (Revonsuo): Dreams rehearse threat responses Evolutionary safety simulator Predictive processing: Dreams = model running offline, updating priors without sensory input
Meditation Neuroscience Default Mode Network (DMN): Active during mind-wandering, self-ref Suppressed during focused attention Focused attention meditation: Strengthens prefrontal control over DMN Alpha/Theta in anterior cingulate Open monitoring (vipassana): Gamma bursts, expanded awareness Non-dual awareness: no self-referential <text x="270" y="304" class="sub" processing" fill="var(--text-muted,#8b949e)" font-size="10">interference. Mirror neurons active. MBSR (Kabat-Zinn): clinical effects Cortical thickness ↑ in long-term meditators
Psychedelic Neuroscience Serotonin 5-HT2A agonism: Psilocybin, LSD, DMT all bind 5-HT2A Destabilizes predictive hierarchies Entropy increase: Carhart-Harris: psychedelics increase neural entropy (less stereotyped patterns) DMN fragmentation = ego dissolution Therapeutic applications: PTSD, depression, addiction Johns Hopkins, Imperial College FDA breakthrough therapy psilocybin
Philosophical Implications of Non-Ordinary States Ordinary waking consciousness is NOT the only form of consciousness — altered states reveal the constructed, modifiable nature of subjective experience. Dream consciousness: phenomenally rich without external input → supports the idea that consciousness is internally generated, not just reactive. Psychedelic ego dissolution: temporary loss of self-boundaries → suggests the "self" is a model, not a fixed metaphysical entity. Connects to Parfit's no-self conclusion. Free resources: Carhart-Harris "The Entropic Brain" (free PDF) · Hobson "The Dreaming Brain" · SEP plato.stanford.edu/entries/consciousness-states/ · Waking up app (Sam Harris)
